XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: ESQFL [7] is the closest prior work in which a secure and explainable quantum federated learning system, powered by digital twins, to assess voltage stability in smart grids. ESQFL asks which client contributed, using Shapley values for participant valuation and allocation within the federation. XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: Once federated and centralized explanations are put on the same client-partition footing (Section 6.7), federated training does not by itself distort quantum model explanations under balanced client data. Under IID and quantity skew, attributions track their centralized equivalents for every encoding that produces a functional model, and round-to-round stability is high in absolute terms. The distortion that does appear is concentrated on Wisconsin and among functional runs, under moderate label skew, and at severe label skew it is entangled with outright collapse. Amplitude encoding has the lowest two-dataset federated-vs-centralized divergence and is among the most stable across rounds (tied with angle). Releasing the explanation vectors is not free: direct membership-inference AUC is resolvably above chance for amplitude, IQP, and re-uploading (and at the boundary of chance for angle), and the noise budget needed to bring it back to near-chance depends on the encoding. A natural objection is that this fidelity result could be circular, an artifact of the federated and centralized models sharing the same low-capacity, four-feature architecture rather than evidence that federation itself preserves explanations; we test that directly with a classical control (Section 8.2).

XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: For anyone deploying explainable quantum federated learning, two things follow. First, noise calibration must be per encoding. The budget that brings angle to near-chance (ε = 1.0) leaves amplitude, re-uploading, and IQP’s leakage largely intact, and bringing all four to near-chance requires a much tighter budget that also degrades explanation utility. A noise level tuned on one encoding does not transfer. Second, explanation release carries a measurable privacy cost even when the model itself is considered safe, and that cost is present across all encodings and both balanced and skewed data. Where the model is functional, quantity skew is the least disruptive non-IID condition for local-to-global divergence. Section 7.4 shows this does not extend to membership leakage, and moderate label skew is the hard case; severe label skew should be expected to remove predictive and explanatory utility together.
XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.after: Two practical qualifications follow. First, the corrected RQ4 results do not identify an effective privacy budget or establish an encoding-dependent leakage ranking. The noise sweep measures explanation distortion, not certified privacy, and should not be used as a deployment protection rule. Second, failure of this particular attack to discriminate membership does not establish safe explanation release: stronger attacks, independent reference data and larger attack samples remain relevant. The RQ3 result is distinct: on Wisconsin, quantity skew stays close to IID in local-to-global distance, while moderate label skew is the most divergent functional condition; severe-skew comparisons remain confounded by collapse and client degeneracy.

XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: The direct membership-inference AUC is a signal-presence proxy, not an attacker-success estimate. The attack classifier is trained and cross-validated on the same target model’s labelled member and non-member explanations, its feature standardization is fit on the pooled set, and member and non-member explanations use training-set and test-set backgrounds respectively. Absolute AUCs are therefore a mild over-estimate and partly sensitive to train/test distribution shift; the cross-encoding ranking and angle’s position at chance are insensitive to both.

Fold-local preprocessing and the common background remove two identified evaluation confounds, but the attack still uses labelled explanations from the same target and a training-derived background. Only one logistic-regression attack family and 100 queried records per target are evaluated. A near-chance estimate does not rule out stronger attacks or certify privacy. Direction-aware and low-FPR diagnostics have substantial finite-sample uncertainty; historical shadow-model scores are not evidence for the corrected protocol.

XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: We asked whether the explanations produced by federated quantum models can be trusted, and measured attribution fidelity, round-to-round stability, local-to-global divergence, and explanation-driven privacy leakage for four quantum encodings on two medical datasets. Answering the question required first correcting a client-to-partition assignment defect and recomputing every federated result, so that federated and centralized explanations are compared like for like. On the corrected results, federating a quantum model does not by itself degrade its feature attributions under balanced client data: under IID and quantity skew, federated attributions track their centralized equivalents and stay stable across rounds. Amplitude and re-uploading both stay functional on both datasets, and amplitude has the lower two-dataset divergence (Pima IID federated-vs-centralized JSD 0.201 ± 0.101 versus re-uploading’s 0.335). This is the one between-encoding fidelity difference resolved at two standard errors, though it is comparable in size to the estimator’s own cross-implementation noise of Section 5.5, within which the Wisconsin cell-to-cell differences fall and the amplitude also ties angle for the most stable attributions at 15 seeds (τ 0.94). Angle collapses on the harder dataset at this circuit size, and IQP is functional there only under IID. Releasing the explanation vectors raises direct membership-inference AUC to 0.53–0.67 across encodings at 15 seeds, amplitude, IQP, and re-uploading are resolvably above chance while angle sits at its boundary, and no single calibrated-noise budget brings all four encodings to near-chance. At ε = 1.0 angle’s AUC falls to 0.415 while the others stay near 0.57, and reaching near-chance for all four requires ε = 0.1. Under severe label skew accuracy and explanation collapse together, driven by the data partition rather than by run-to-run variation. The most transferable claim is amplitude’s two-dataset fidelity; the remainder is anchored to Wisconsin and should be read as such.

XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.after: The corrected clean IID evaluation does not reproduce the earlier encoding-dependent membership-leakage ranking. XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: Two features of the direct attack qualify these AUCs. The attack classifier’s feature standardization is fit on the pooled member and non-member set before cross-validation, so the absolute AUCs are a mild over-estimate; this is uniform across encodings and seeds and does not affect the cross-encoding gaps or the angle-versus-chance test. And member explanations are computed against a training-set background while non-member explanations use a test-set background, so a portion of the measured separability could reflect train/test input-distribution shift carried through the background rather than model memorization of members; angle remaining at chance bounds that portion as small. XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.before: The calibrated-Laplace-noise sweep covers four encodings, four budgets, and five seeds on Wisconsin IID (Table 5, Figure 7). Noise is added to the Q-SHAP vectors post hoc with the model held fixed across budgets for each encoding-seed pair, so this traces the privacy-utility curve of explanation release, not of a retrained private model. Figure 7 plots the same sweep against the retained explanation utility rather than the budget label, so the release cost is read directly in explanation degradation. At ε = 0.1 all encodings fall to AUC 0.311 to 0.331, uniformly near random. At ε = 1.0 angle’s AUC falls to 0.415 while amplitude, re-uploading, and IQP sit at 0.562 to 0.588. AUC rises monotonically with ε for 19 of 20 encoding-seed pairs (the one exception, angle seed 123, dips 0.002 at ε = 5.0, within permutation-sampling variance). No single budget brings all encodings equally close to chance: bringing all four to near-chance requires ε = 0.1. A deployment that set ε = 1.0 from angle’s response alone would leave the other three encodings about 15 points higher.
XQFL_paper_humanized.docx.after: The corrected noise sweep holds each target fixed across release settings and measures utility on exactly the vectors scored by the attack (Table 5, Figure 7). It does not reproduce monotonic leakage suppression. At epsilon = 0.1, mean raw AUCs span 0.463–0.512, rather than the earlier below-chance values. One noisy cell, IQP at epsilon = 1, has AUC 0.561 ± 0.051 and exceeds chance by approximately 2.65 SE; this is an isolated, unadjusted comparison among the tested cells, not a stable encoding ranking or evidence for a mitigation mechanism. Neither a universal effective epsilon nor encoding-specific required privacy budgets are established.

PAPER_FORMAT/XQFL_IEEE_Transactions_Form.before: Abstract—Federated learning allows several data holders train a shared model without ever pooling their raw data. Quantum machine learning offers a different computational model for small-data classification. Whether the explanations produced by the combined system stay faithful, stable, and safe to release has not been asked, and answering it first requires comparing federated and reference explanations on a like-for-like basis. We evaluate Explainable Quantum Federated Learning (XQFL) across four quantum encodings (angle, amplitude, data re-uploading, and IQP) on the Wisconsin Breast Cancer and Pima Indians Diabetes datasets, computing Shapley-value explanations for centralized and federated models across training rounds and heterogeneous client distributions. Amplitude gives the strongest two-dataset attribution fidelity (Pima IID federated-vs-centralized JSD 0.201 ± 0.101 versus re-uploading’s 0.335). That gap resolves at two standard errors, and it is the only between-encoding fidelity difference this study settles. It is no larger than the estimator’s own cross-implementation noise, and on Wisconsin the between-encoding differences fall inside that noise. Amplitude and angle tie for round-to-round stability (Kendall’s τ 0.94), ahead of re-uploading (0.89) and IQP (0.86). Among functional runs on Wisconsin, moderate label skew (α = 0.5) shows the largest local-to-global explanation divergence while quantity skew stays close to IID, and severe label skew is confounded with model collapse. Direct membership-inference AUC on the explanation vectors is highest for re-uploading (0.665) and closest to chance for angle (0.533, not resolved above chance). Amplitude, IQP, and re-uploading each sit resolvably above angle, and calibrated Laplace noise suppresses this leakage unevenly and no single budget brings every encoding to near chance. On the harder dataset, angle collapses at this circuit size while IQP remains functional only under IID.

ESQFL asks which client contributed, using Shapley values for participant valuation and allocation within the federation. PAPER_FORMAT/XQFL_IEEE_Transactions_Form.before: For anyone deploying explainable quantum federated learning, two things follow. First, noise calibration must be per encoding. The budget that brings angle to near-chance (ε = 1.0) leaves amplitude, re-uploading, and IQP’s leakage largely intact, and bringing all four to near-chance requires a much tighter budget that also degrades explanation utility. A noise level tuned on one encoding does not transfer. PAPER_FORMAT/XQFL_IEEE_Transactions_Form.after: Two practical qualifications follow. First, the corrected RQ4 results do not identify an effective privacy budget or establish an encoding-dependent leakage ranking. The noise sweep measures explanation distortion, not certified privacy, and should not be used as a deployment protection rule. Second, failure of this particular attack to discriminate membership does not establish safe explanation release: stronger attacks, independent reference data and larger attack samples remain relevant. The RQ3 result is distinct: on Wisconsin, quantity skew stays close to IID in local-to-global distance, while moderate label skew is the most divergent functional condition; severe-skew comparisons remain confounded by collapse and client degeneracy.

PAPER_FORMAT/XQFL_IEEE_Transactions_Form.before: We asked whether the explanations produced by federated quantum models can be trusted, and measured attribution fidelity, round-to-round stability, local-to-global divergence, and explanation-driven privacy leakage for four quantum encodings on two medical datasets. Answering the question required first correcting a client-to-partition assignment defect and recomputing every federated result, so that federated and centralized explanations are compared like for like. On the corrected results, federating a quantum model does not by itself degrade its feature attributions under balanced client data: under IID and quantity skew, federated attributions track their centralized equivalents and stay stable across rounds. Amplitude and re-uploading both stay functional on both datasets, and amplitude has the lower two-dataset divergence (Pima IID federated-vs-centralized JSD 0.201 ± 0.101 versus re-uploading’s 0.335). This is the one between-encoding fidelity difference resolved at two standard errors, though it is comparable in size to the estimator’s own cross-implementation noise of Section V-E, within which the Wisconsin cell-to-cell differences fall and the amplitude also ties angle for the most stable attributions at 15 seeds (τ 0.94). Angle collapses on the harder dataset at this circuit size, and IQP is functional there only under IID. Releasing the explanation vectors raises direct membership-inference AUC to 0.53–0.67 across encodings at 15 seeds, amplitude, IQP, and re-uploading are resolvably above chance while angle sits at its boundary, and no single calibrated-noise budget brings all four encodings to near-chance. At ε = 1.0 angle’s AUC falls to 0.415 while the others stay near 0.57, and reaching near-chance for all four requires ε = 0.1. Under severe label skew accuracy and explanation collapse together, driven by the data partition rather than by run-to-run variation. The most transferable claim is amplitude’s two-dataset fidelity; the remainder is anchored to Wisconsin and should be read as such.

PAPER_FORMAT/XQFL_IEEE_Transactions_Form.before: Two features of the direct attack qualify these AUCs.
